scope.summary: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh index-rebuild-suite evidence proves the complete requirement: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.

[positive] Execute every named supported behavior and prove from canonical state: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.

[negative] Malformed, unsupported, stale, unauthorized, or boundary-crossing variants cannot produce false success for: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.

[failure_recovery] Interrupt and restart at each durable boundary; completed truth is preserved and the requirement converges without duplication: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.

[concurrency] Parallel actors/jobs retain isolated identity, bounded execution, deterministic conflict handling, and attributable receipts while satisfying: Index rebuild, corruption recovery, retention, URL normalization, ranking, and semantic-query boundary are deterministic.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
Legacy Stage code (WP-12) must not silently constrain this MT (STAGE-DEC-017).
Do not duplicate ArtifactStore, WP-1 ToolGate/process/promotion, or Loom authority.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
